issues.description: Unaddressed common method variance: The study design relies exclusively on cross-sectional self-report data to measure behavioral frequency, moral disapproval, and perceived addiction. This approach is highly susceptible to common method variance (CMV), which can artificially inflate or suppress relationships between variables. Given that the behaviors under investigation carry varying degrees of social stigma and legal status (e.g., illicit drug use versus alcohol consumption), CMV and social desirability bias may differentially impact the reporting of moral disapproval and addiction symptoms across categories. The authors should discuss how CMV might influence the comparative moderation analyses and whether it could confound the attempt to isolate the unique effect of moral incongruence for pornography.

issues.description: Unvalidated ASSIST modification: The authors propose modifying the NIDA-ASSIST to include pornography and gambling to facilitate parallel analyses across all behaviors. While the inclusion of the Brief Pornography Screen and the Problem Gambling Severity Index provides validated alternatives, relying on an unvalidated adaptation of a substance-use screening tool for behavioral addictions introduces significant psychometric uncertainty into the parallel analyses. The cognitive interpretation of "urges" or "health, social, legal, or financial problems" may function differently for substance use versus pornography viewing. The manuscript should explicitly discuss the limitations of assuming measurement invariance across these distinct behavioral and chemical domains when comparing the magnitude of interaction effects.
issues.quote: We will also include pornography and gambling as response options on the NIDA-ASSIST, in addition to the measures listed above. These will be included to allow fully parallel analysis across behaviors and substances (i.e., everything will be on the exact same scale using the exact same measurements). Although such an approach is not currently validated for gambling or pornography, given the inclusion of other validated scales to assess these outcomes (see below), including them within the NIDA-ASSIST will not decrement our ability to evaluate our key hypotheses.

issues.description: Reliability of single-item moderators: The proposed design relies on a single-item measure to assess moral disapproval across all evaluated behaviors. Single-item measures generally exhibit lower reliability than multi-item scales, which systematically attenuates the observable effect size of interaction terms in ordinary least squares regression. Because the analytic plan relies on equivalence testing to demonstrate a practical null effect for non-sexual behaviors, attenuated interaction effects due to measurement error could result in falsely concluding that moral incongruence is unique to pornography. The authors should address how potential differences in the reliability of this single item across different behaviors might impact the equivalence tests, and consider discussing this as a limitation or proposing a sensitivity analysis adjusting for assumed reliability.
issues.quote: Additionally, we will include a series of single-item moral disapproval questions that match previous measures of moral disapproval of pornography. For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement “I believe that using ________ is morally wrong” on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.description: Contradictory survey routing logic: The manuscript contains a critical contradiction regarding the administration of the problematic use measures. On page 6, the text states that "only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use." However, on page 7, the text claims that "key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior." This discrepancy fundamentally alters the sample size, degrees of freedom, and statistical distribution of the dependent variables. Including non-users will likely result in severe zero-inflation and heavily skew the interaction terms. Please clarify the exact inclusion criteria for the regression models and ensure the survey routing logic is consistently described.

issues.description: Unspecified alternative statistical models: For a Registered Report, vaguely stating that supplemental analyses will be conducted if OLS assumptions are violated is insufficient. Given that the dependent variables (e.g., modified NIDA-ASSIST scores) measure problematic substance use in a general population, the data are highly likely to be right-skewed or zero-inflated. To prevent researcher degrees of freedom during the Stage 2 analysis, the authors must explicitly pre-specify the exact alternative models (e.g., negative binomial regression, zero-inflated Poisson, or robust standard errors) that will be employed if the assumptions of linearity, homoscedasticity, or normality of residuals are violated.

issues.description: Domain-specific equivalence bounds: The authors justify their Smallest Effect Size of Interest (SESOI) for equivalence testing based entirely on prior literature examining pornography use. Applying this specific standardized estimate as the equivalence bound for entirely different behaviors (e.g., illicit drug use, gambling) assumes that the measurement reliability, base rates, and clinical relevance of a standardized unit change are identical across these domains. An effect size that is practically meaningless for pornography might be clinically relevant for illicit substance use, or vice versa. The authors should justify why an effect size derived from sexual behavior is the appropriate threshold for declaring an effect practically zero in the context of substance use and gambling disorders, or alternatively, establish domain-specific SESOIs.

issues.description: Confounding from gambling oversample: The study design combines a nationally representative sample (n=2,500) with a massive oversample of sports wagerers (n=1,500). Because the primary analyses compare the effects of moral incongruence across different behaviors (pornography vs. gambling vs. substances), this oversample introduces a severe confound. The combined sample will be heavily skewed toward individuals who gamble, who likely possess systematically different moral evaluations of gambling, different baseline rates of addiction, and potentially different demographic or psychological profiles compared to the general population. Without a plan to apply survey weights or analyze the representative and oversampled groups separately, it will be impossible to determine whether differences in the predictive power of moral incongruence between gambling and other behaviors are true behavioral differences or merely artifacts of the skewed sample composition.

This will provide us with a total sample of over 4,000 American adults.

issues.description: Inconsistent behavioral frequency scaling: The manuscript states that pornography frequency will be measured on a scale of 1 to 6, whereas the modified NIDA-ASSIST frequency for substances is described earlier as being on a scale of 0 to 5. While this may be a simple coding discrepancy, comparing interaction terms across different behaviors requires that the constituent variables be scaled and centered identically. If the frequency metrics possess different absolute scales or different functional distributions (e.g., normal vs. heavily zero-inflated), the resulting interaction coefficients cannot be directly compared to establish the uniqueness of the pornography effect. The analytic plan should explicitly detail how these frequency distributions will be harmonized or standardized prior to computing the interaction terms and conducting the equivalence tests.

issues.description: Unaddressed range restriction in moderators: The authors hypothesize that the interaction between moral disapproval and behavioral frequency will be significant for pornography but practically zero for gambling and substance use. However, the logical conclusion that moral incongruence is unique to sexual behavior relies on the assumption that moral disapproval is distributed similarly across all tested behaviors. It is highly probable that behaviors like alcohol or cannabis use have significantly lower base rates and narrower variances of moral disapproval compared to pornography use. If the variance of the moderator (moral disapproval) is severely restricted for substance use, the interaction term will naturally be attenuated or null. To logically support the claim of uniqueness, the authors must include a plan to assess and account for differences in the base rates and variances of moral disapproval across the different behavioral domains.
